title: White Garlic Chicken Pizza
seoTitle: White Garlic Chicken Pizza | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Creamy white pie, roasted garlic
description: Creamy white pie, roasted garlic. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Proof the dough
steps.instruction: Stir yeast into warm water with a pinch of sugar; bloom 5 minutes until foamy. Mix flour, salt, oil, and yeast water until a shaggy dough forms. Knead 8–10 minutes until smooth. Rise covered 1–1½ hours until doubled — White Garlic Chicken Pizza needs relaxed gluten for an open crumb.

steps.title: Heat oven and stone
steps.instruction: Place a pizza stone or inverted sheet pan in the oven. Preheat to 500°F for at least 45 minutes — surface temp matters more than air temp. Prep sauce and cheese while the oven saturates.

steps.title: Stretch and top
steps.instruction: Divide dough; stretch by hand (don't roll with a pin unless Detroit-style). Sauce lightly — wet centers sag. Add cheese and toppings. Work on parchment or floured peel; jiggle to confirm it slides.

steps.title: Bake until blistered
steps.instruction: Slide onto the hot stone. Bake 10–14 minutes until cheese bubbles with brown spots and the underside sounds hollow when tapped. Rotate once if your oven has hot spots.

steps.title: Rest and cut
steps.instruction: Rest 2 minutes before cutting so cheese sets. Cut on sheet trays for the hall line. Hold backup pies at 200°F uncovered up to 15 minutes — covering traps steam and softens crust.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold protein after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Cut pies into hall slices (8 per pie minimum) and fan on sheet trays.
Keep a fresh pie warming in the oven — pizza dies fast on the counter.
Line up White Garlic Chicken Pizza on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Creamy white pie, roasted garlic. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
